name: CorVel Corporation (ADJACENT - specialist risk services: claims & managed care)

geography.fx_notes: US-only operations (workers' comp, auto, liability, health payment integrity).

kpis.name: Organic growth
kpis.value: Company does not report organic separately; acquisitions historically immaterial - reported growth used as proxy (not substituted into organic field)

management.succession_notes: Founder V. Gordon Clemons remains Chairman (not re-verified)

ownership.controlling_holders: Founder/Chairman V. Gordon Clemons and affiliates are large holders - % not extracted

evidence: Recurring claims administration, bill review and network contracts with employers/TPAs/insurers (S1)
A.rationale: Contracted, multi-year service relationships; volume linked to employment/claims.

evidence: Integrated managed-care + TPA platform; new Top-10 health plan win (S2)
B.rationale: Proprietary integrated platform and networks create switching costs.

evidence: NI margin ~12% TTM, ROIC high with zero debt (S1)
C.rationale: Scale in workers' comp managed care shows in rising margins.

evidence: CERiS health payment integrity expanding to Top-10 plans and BCBS market (S2)
D.rationale: Under-penetrated runway in health payment integrity.

evidence: Consistent growth and buybacks; no guidance given (S2)
Zero debt; continual buybacks ($18.1m Q2 FY27) (S2)
Bill review, claims admin and case management (S1)
I1.rationale: Bill review/claims processing automatable by AI (risk and opportunity); nurse case management more resilient (INFERENCE).

evidence: Mix of per-claim fees and % of savings (INFERENCE)
No adjusted EPS; GAAP reporting, net cash (S1,S2)

ai.notes: Company markets AI/ML/NLP in claims handling (S1).

sector_specific.organic_ex_rate_note: Not a broker: revenue is fee/volume-based (claims, bills, network savings), not tied to premium rates. Reported growth ~7-13% p.a.

gates.notes: Net cash. Customer concentration not disclosed in sources used. Adjacent subgroup (specialist risk services).

bull_points: Debt-free compounder with double-digit growth and steady buybacks.
CERiS health payment integrity adds a large new runway.
bear_points: G&A growing faster than revenue for two quarters.
AI-native claims/bill-review entrants could commoditise core services.
US workers' comp claim frequency structurally declining.
thesis_breakers: Revenue growth < 5% for a fiscal year.
Operating margin declines two consecutive years.
